sources: Stereogum (Tom Breihan, 2013): "Debut didn't just establish Björk; it helped make sounds like that cool to a segment of the music-dork universe that might've remained deaf to its charms otherwise"; "it's virtually impossible to imagine a big publication slamming an adventurous dance-pop album for 'cheap electronic gimmickry,' and Debut is a big part of that change" https://www.stereogum.com/1398922/bjorks-debut-turns-20/top-stories/

Rolling Stone, 500 Greatest Albums of All Time (2020): ranked No. 202, "has enraptured countless artists, from Thom Yorke to Arca, in the years since its release" https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-albums-of-all-time-1062063/bjork-homogenic-1063031/ | Pitchfork, The 150 Best Albums of the 1990s (2022): ranked No. 6 https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/the-best-albums-of-the-1990s/ | Loud and Quiet (Sam Walton, 2017): "it also resembles a modern template for successful artistic reinvention"; "The internal paradoxes of Kanye West's '808s And Heartbreak', for example, seem to echo those on 'Homogenic'" https://www.loudandquiet.com/short/bjork-homogenic-at-20-template-for-artistic-reinvention

Crack Magazine (2024): "you can hear its influence elsewhere: in the pops and clicks of Timbaland’s vocal-forward, mid-2000s productions ...; in the eerie primordialism of Gazelle Twin’s Pastoral; and in Holly Herndon’s PROTO – an album of glitchy choral work and high-concept technofeminism that is possibly Medúlla’s greatest successor" https://crackmagazine.net/article/long-reads/bjorks-medulla-retrospective/
